Recruiters often spend less than 10 seconds reviewing an application, so presenting your qualifications in the right format is essential.In this complete guide, you’ll learn everything about CVs, resumes, their differences, formats, and best practices to help you create a professional document that stands out in today’s competitive job market.What Is a CV?A CV (Curriculum Vitae) is a comprehensive document that provides a detailed overview of your educational background, professional experience, skills, certifications, research, projects, publications, and career achievements.The term Curriculum Vitae comes from Latin and translates to “Course of Life.”Unlike a resume, a CV is designed to present your complete academic and professional journey rather than a brief summary.Why Is a CV Important?A professional CV helps employers understand your qualifications and determine whether you’re a suitable candidate for a position.A well-written CV can:Create a strong first impressionHighlight your qualificationsShowcase your professional achievementsImprove interview opportunitiesDemonstrate career progressionPresent your skills in a structured formatWhat Is a Resume?A Resume is a concise document that summarizes your most relevant qualifications for a specific job.Unlike a CV, a resume is typically limited to one or two pages and is customized for each application.Its primary objective is to quickly demonstrate why you’re the right candidate for a particular role.CV vs Resume: Key DifferencesFeatureCVResumeFull FormCurriculum VitaeResumeLength2–5+
